reconcile.connective: Matthew Henry answers the timing worry by relocating 'paradise' to Hades, the realm of separated souls, distinct from the Father's heaven reached at the ascension.

discrepancy.connective: The Skeptics' Annotated Bible's Steve Wells presses the plain sense: Luke puts Jesus in paradise that day; John still has him un-ascended three days later.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Did Jesus go to heaven after he died but before his ascension?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/visit.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013), contra page "Did Jesus go to heaven after he died but before his ascension?"

excerpts.excerpt_text: Christ here lets us know that he was going to paradise himself, to hades - the invisible world. His human soul was removing to the place of separate souls; not to the place of the damned, but to paradise, the place of the blessed.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers the paradise-vs-ascension timing worry by identifying 'paradise' with Hades/the intermediate state of separated souls, not with the Father's heaven that Jesus later says he has not yet entered.

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874), pp. 198-199
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley quotes Luke 23:43's 'to-day...in paradise' directly against a 'not yet ascended' text (Acts 2:34) and resolves it exactly as Matthew Henry does: the paradise promise names the disembodied intermediate state, distinct from the full heavenly reward reached after resurrection and ascension.

link.title: GotQuestions: What did Jesus mean when He said, "Today you will be with me in paradise"?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment of the paradise-vs-still-dead-body timing question (spirit/body distinction); does not name John 20:17 explicitly.
